finding: tests/test_review.py:425 The Markdown inertness test does not contain a standalone bare URL.
rationale: AC6 explicitly requires bare HTTP(S) autolink coverage, but the only tested URLs are structurally embedded and arbitrary dataset statements can reach report serialization, so no upstream guard makes a standalone URL unreachable; the current generic escaping regex is fail-safe today but does not replace the missing behavioral regression proof.

evidence.output: The locked acceptance criterion says "Dataset-derived Markdown is inert, including bare URL autolinks." The task gate records clean=true and green=true at 4a1746f9050120df52e7845166f0ab935c4e584a.

The only input occurrences are line 432, "Acme [click](https://example.invalid/pixel)", and line 433, ""; lines 450-453 only assert those constructs and the shared raw substring are absent. There is no standalone prose URL anywhere in the file.

draft_findings copies signal['statement'] without a URL-shape restriction, accept_findings promotes that statement, and write_report passes it to _markdown_text. Thus a standalone dataset URL is reachable from the same public path exercised by the test.

_markdown_text currently neutralizes every word-boundary HTTP(S) scheme with re.sub(r'(?i)\bhttps?://', ...) after generic Markdown escaping. This makes the present implementation fail safe, but it is not an upstream impossibility guard and the existing embedded-only fixture would also pass an implementation that removed link/image constructs while leaving standalone autolinks active.
